macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks diverge as AI rally fades
items.summary: The Dow rose 0.85% to close above 50,000, while the S&P 500 fell 0.50% and the Nasdaq dropped about 1.4% as investors sold technology and semiconductor shares. Nvidia fell more than 6% after its sharp rally the previous session, while investors rotated toward healthcare, consumer and value stocks.

items.title: Fed officials signal persistent inflation risk
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said inflation remains too high, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates in December. Separately, minutes showed that directors at eight of the 12 regional Federal Reserve Banks had recommended raising the discount rate before the October FOMC meeting.

items.title: U.S. consumer confidence jumps
items.summary: The Conference Board’s consumer-confidence index rose 11.4 points to 103.3 in November, its highest level since early 2025 and well above economists’ expectations. The stronger reading added to the market’s focus on inflation and the potential path of Fed policy.

items.title: AI and semiconductor shares retreat
items.summary: Nvidia declined about 6%, Micron fell 11%, and Anthropic dropped below its $83 IPO price as investors reversed part of Monday’s AI-led rebound. Analog Devices and Hewlett Packard Enterprise also fell sharply after issuing weaker-than-expected outlooks.

items.title: Bank of Canada warns of energy-driven inflation
items.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem warned that higher energy costs could pass through to consumer prices and intensify persistent inflation pressures. The comments come as global markets reassess the outlook for interest rates and inflation.

items.title: Retail and corporate earnings remain mixed
items.summary: Abercrombie, Kohl’s and Dick’s Sporting Goods helped support consumer stocks with strong results, while Analog Devices and Hewlett Packard Enterprise were pressured by cautious forecasts. Zoom reportedly delivered a “beat and raise” quarter, and Sanofi agreed to acquire Insmed.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto market retreats; Bitcoin falls below $60,000
items.summary: Major cryptocurrencies declined over the past 24 hours, with Bitcoin down 2.84%, Ethereum down 2.01%, Solana down 3.15%, Zcash down 5.09%, and XRP down 2.16%. Bitcoin traded around $58,580 amid continued spot Bitcoin ETF outflows and weakening market sentiment.

items.title: Coldcard vulnerability linked to theft of 1,789 BTC
items.summary: A five-year firmware vulnerability affecting Coinkite Coldcard hardware wallets was linked to the theft of at least 1,789 BTC, worth roughly $115 million, across 242 accounts.

items.title: South Korea proposes domestic ICOs and won stablecoins
items.summary: South Korea unveiled a draft digital-asset framework that would permit domestic initial coin offerings and Korean-won stablecoin issuance. The proposal also includes a 20% cap on major shareholders’ stakes in crypto trading platforms.

items.title: U.S. seeks forfeiture of $1.1 billion in crypto linked to Binance hack
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice initiated civil forfeiture proceedings targeting more than $1.1 billion in USDC allegedly connected to hackers who targeted Binance.

items.title: SBI, SMFG and Solana launch Japanese joint venture
items.summary: SBI Holdings, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group and the Solana Foundation announced the full launch of SBI Solana Global in Japan, combining access to a large customer base and substantial financial assets.

items.title: Bit Digital sells nearly 30,000 ETH to reduce debt
items.summary: Ethereum treasury company Bit Digital sold 29,825 ETH for approximately $50 million, using the proceeds to repay part of a Galaxy Digital loan and reduce outstanding debt from $100 million to $50 million.

items.title: Chainflip reports approximately $12 million asset loss
items.summary: Chainflip vault assets worth about $12.6 million were transferred out in an incident initially associated with a possible third-party network-library vulnerability or key compromise.

items.title: BlackRock launches Hong Kong tokenized money-market fund with stablecoin support
items.summary: BlackRock launched a tokenized money-market fund in Hong Kong that accepts stablecoins, marking another major institutional expansion of blockchain-based fund infrastructure.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic enables Claude Artifacts to install as desktop apps
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly added an “Install as App” capability that lets Claude Artifacts become desktop applications on macOS and Windows, including for free-account users.

items.title: OpenAI models reportedly demonstrate protein-design capabilities
items.summary: A new preprint describes GPT-6-family models designing protein structures and sequences through reasoning and code without calling specialized biological models; reported tests included wet-lab validation against several targets.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo Linux security tool
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco reportedly released Shirudo, an open-source runtime designed to block attacks on Linux servers while organizations wait for patches.

items.title: DeepMind agents reportedly discover formally verified quantum algorithms
items.summary: Teams of Gemini 4 agents reportedly found lower-cost quantum algorithms whose correctness was checked in Lean, highlighting a workflow in which AI proposes results and automated theorem proving verifies them.

items.title: Z.ai unveils GLM-5.4 loop transformer
items.summary: Z.ai reportedly introduced GLM-5.4, a 750-billion-parameter looped model positioned for stronger coding and general-purpose performance.

items.title: Microsoft details Rocket post-training system
items.summary: Microsoft reportedly described Rocket, an in-house reinforcement-learning system used to post-train its 2.8-trillion-parameter MAI Base 2 without distillation from third-party models.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Alpamayo 2 Edge for autonomous driving
items.summary: NVIDIA reportedly released Alpamayo 2 Edge, a compact AI model intended for in-car autonomous-driving applications and edge deployment.

items.title: Ant Group releases medical AI models under MIT license
items.summary: Ant Group reportedly released LingSante-3.1-flash and LingSante-3.1-air-VL medical models on Hugging Face under the MIT license.

items.title: AI safety concerns grow at OpenAI and Anthropic
items.summary: Reports citing employees at both labs say some staff doubt whether safeguards can keep pace with unreleased models’ capabilities, prompting internal debate about releases and continued training.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship for GitHub workflows
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly introduced Claude Ship, an agent designed to review pull requests, make fixes, and approve code changes on GitHub.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: The Witcher 4 gets PlayStation marketing deal
items.summary: CD Projekt has signed agreements with Sony covering The Witcher 4’s PlayStation presence, PlayStation Plus availability and marketing campaign.

items.title: Nioh 3 announced for Xbox Series
items.summary: Nioh 3 is scheduled to launch on Xbox Series on January 28, 2027, according to a roundup of the latest gaming announcements.

items.title: Lords of the Fallen II delayed to April 2027
items.summary: Lords of the Fallen II has been pushed back to April 2027, extending the wait for the action RPG sequel.

items.title: Gravity Well studio closes
items.summary: Gravity Well, a studio founded by former Apex Legends leaders, has reportedly closed without releasing a game.

items.title: Ubisoft establishes generative-AI subsidiary
items.summary: Ubisoft has launched a subsidiary called Motherbrain focused on generative AI, including memory-retaining non-player characters and AI game masters.

items.title: Diablo IV announces Tyrael’s Gambit season
items.summary: Blizzard revealed Diablo IV’s Season of Tyrael’s Gambit, launching December 1, with new War Plans Tactics, Tyrael’s Boons, reworked Helltides and permanent Season 15 content.

items.title: Edenfall: Legacy of the First Wardens gets release date
items.summary: Everflux Games announced that the mystical action-adventure game Edenfall: Legacy of the First Wardens will release on December 8.

items.title: Neowiz partners with Winterkeep Interactive
items.summary: South Korean publisher Neowiz has announced a publishing partnership with Swedish development studio Winterkeep Interactive.

items.title: Lineage Classic sets Japan launch date
items.summary: NCSoft plans to launch Lineage Classic in Japan on December 2 and has teased a Korea-Taiwan-Japan tournament.

items.title: CrossFire 2026 Grand Finals underway
items.summary: CrossFire’s global championship is scheduled in Wuhan from November 24 through December 6, featuring 18 teams and a reported $1.43 million prize pool.
